summary: We designed a story-driven educational game; children are more likely to understand a concept explained through gameplay than websites that flood their mind with info that’s why we designed a simple 2D top down game with minigames inspired from real NASA missions and equipment left on Mars and the Moon with questions two different and unique chapters one on the moon and one on Mars the story is philosophical as you start playing with an engineer who thinks looking at past equipment takes too much effort and is just better to make new ones that are better but his mindset slowly changes as we realize things worth aren’t just because of what they can do but because of what they did as the lessons we learnt from them can never be forgotten  which I believe is the core of our challenge and we made scientific accurate minigames at each mission to explain concepts or ideas in a simple way and the player slowly learns these weren’t just equipment they are our past we learn from and the base our future is built on the player also learns a lot of info about each one of them throughout his gameplay and cut scenes which are rich in info while having a logical and simple story you don’t just learn what the machines did you experience it yourself  I think it is important because it is so easy to use and can be played world wide and it is easy for kids all around the world to understand while teaching them real missions through simplified gameplay and cut scenes to make it interactive
details: Our project is an educational 2D game you play as an astronaut sent on a mission to investigate and examine NASA’s equipment left on mars but a failure in the landing system leads you to crash before contacting earth which barley communicates with you before putting a lunar team to guide you through your journey your character starts the game thinking equipment lose their worth the moment their mission ends and that it is better to make new equipment than examine old ones but the more you play the more he changes as he realizes these aren’t just tools or equipment; they are our history a reflection of their creator and the human will which sometimes exceeds expectations and at the end he realize they are priceless as I just explained and they are a lesson we learn from and base to build our future and each piece reflects the one who made it and through out the game you learn a lot of information about these equipment the game consists of machines 5 on mars and 2 on the moon each mission includes cut scenes that explain everything and the story of these pieces of equipment and a game that is scientifically accurate and inspired from real NASA missions and the concept of simplifying difficult concepts into easy to understand fun interactive games which fits this challenge best knowing our target is school age kids and teenagers and because this is a game it will attract way more users than a website and it can be accessed from anywhere at the world with no cost and it is so easy to apply in real life and we can add other languages in the future to attract more people isn’t just for kids it’s for all ages but kids and teenagers will like it most because of its bright colors fun gameplay and interactive learning ways our project really shines in simplifying difficult concepts through interactive games or cut scenes and a good story about an astronaut changing his mind from seeing the mission as useless like most do to identifying the importance of looking at our past and learning which is the core concept of the challenge itself and this changes the player point of view a lot as he can finally understand these equipment know how they work information like when did they launch and their objectives and most importantly why he should even care for something like this and we must remember the challenge talked about leaving a connection between the user and these equipment which we do through the story of the astronaut and it’s sad ending as the rescue team can’t arrive because of a dust storm making him trapped on mars although on Earth he is remembered as a hero which begs the question does equipment and even humans lose their worth once they can’t provide anymore? And the answer actually is in both the game and the challenge as our main character ends up abandoned but never forgotten and the games accurately represent the equipment's real functions, discoveries, and limitations
dataRefs: We used the NASA resources provided in the official challenge page as the main source of information for our project. These materials helped us understand the history, objectives, functions, discoveries, and scientific contributions of the equipment featured in our game. We used this information to create historically grounded missions, educational minigames, and cutscenes that explain the real NASA missions in an engaging and accessible way.  No additional external data sources were used.
